about.title: Riverside Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails should never have reached your hands in the first place. Yet in a city of 322,424 people, Riverside households buy space heaters, e-bikes, power tools, car seats, medications and countless other goods every day, trusting that each one was designed, built and labeled with care. When that trust breaks, whether a battery ignites in a Canyon Crest garage or a tire separates during the Friday evening commute on I-215 or SR-91, the harm lands on ordinary people rather than on the company that shipped the item. California law recognizes this. Under strict liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You need to show the product had a design, manufacturing or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Responsibility can reach the maker, the distributor and the retailer alike. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects injured Riverside County residents with an independent personal injury attorney who takes product cases on contingency. Hold onto the product, its packaging and any receipts, and let us make the introduction.

whyChoose.title: Why Riverside Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict liability works in your favor
items.desc: In most California product cases you do not have to prove the company was negligent. Showing a design, manufacturing or warning defect that caused your injury is generally the heart of the claim, and the attorneys we connect you with know how to build that showing.

items.title: Every link in the chain can be accountable
items.desc: California allows claims against the manufacturer, the distributor and the retailer who sold the item. That matters when a maker is overseas or out of business and a Riverside store or regional distributor is closer to home.

items.title: Preserving the product is step one
items.desc: The failed item is often the single most important piece of evidence, so an attorney will want it kept unaltered and unrepaired. We make a fast, free connection so that guidance reaches you before anything is thrown away.

items.question: My tire came apart on SR-91 through Riverside and I was hurt. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. Riverside recorded 1,995 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those involved equipment that failed rather than a driver who erred. If a tire, brake component or airbag was defective, a strict liability claim against the manufacturer, distributor or seller may exist alongside any claim involving another driver. Keep the vehicle and the failed part exactly as they are until an attorney has looked at them.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Generally, no. Under California's strict liability approach, the focus is on whether the product had a defect in its design, its manufacturing or its warnings and whether that defect caused your injury. You typically do not need to show what the company knew or how careful it was. An independent attorney can explain which theory fits your situation.

items.question: I threw away the box but still have the broken product. Does that matter?
items.answer: The product itself is the priority, so hold onto it and do not attempt repairs or send it back to the seller. Packaging, manuals, receipts, photos of the scene and medical records all help, but a missing box rarely ends a claim. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and the attorney we connect you with works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.
